speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you presented with right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly what you mean by "abnormal leg positioning"?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did your leg get stuck in a fixed position, such as pointing straight up, immediately after the crash? Also, were you wearing a seatbelt when the collision occurred?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Hip Dislocation (Posterior).

The clinical picture of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated right leg following trauma is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. Given the severity of the injury, please hold while I request imaging to confirm the location of the femoral head.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hip_XRay
